Sale Qualification occurs when the Sales Executive has validated that the client is a good fit for the product being sold and a good fit to work with ATG. They engage the Solution Engineer, conduct knowledge transfer, and complete introductions with the Client.

Sales to Delivery Handoff occurs once the SOW is executed and the delivery team is staffed. To prepare for the meeting, the delivery team researches the client and reviews artifacts provided from the sales cycle. The deal team facilitates the meeting and covers company overview, project overview, and any key risks or issues.

Prior to client kickoff, the assessment team develops an initial discovery plan based on the signed SOW, information from the sales cycle, and the team's own client research and review of artifacts. This discovery plan is reviewed by ATG leadership prior to the first scheduled discovery session to ensure the team is prepared for a comprehensive discovery process.

Project Success Confirmation occurs once workshop sessions are done and some planning and design is complete. The project and deal team work internally to ensure there is alignment between what was scoped and what was discovered in workshop sessions. Then, ATG meets with the client to present any discrepancies and align on corrective actions to ensure project success.

CoE and Delivery Sign Off is the exit criteria for this stage. Once the Project Team finalizes the effort as per the CoE estimation templates, and identifies deviations (if any), the same are verified by the CoE and Delivery Leadership before this is taken forward to the implementation phase.

Configuration and Test Plan Sign Off occurs once all build is completed. The purpose of configuration sign off is to officially get client's agreement that all critical business requirements have been met, which is critical piece of scope management. The purpose of Test Plan sign off is to confirm that all aspects needed for a successful UAT session are in place, such as UAT test cases, end user training, end user communications, and a feedback mechanism. The client typically owns these activities with ATG supporting , but ownership varies based on the project.

As the assessment team approaches the end of the discovery process and begins deeper analysis of findings, the team prepares for an interim readout to share their findings, including key observations and themes, with the client. Prior to the interim readout, the team holds a rehearsal with ATG leadership and relevant SMEs to pressure test the content and talk track.

Go / No-Go typically occurs at a fixed date at the end of the UAT period. This decision includes stakeholders, executives, and business process owners. The purpose is to have final acceptance and closure of UAT, even if there may be outstanding work to resolve high priority defects.

As the team approaches the end of the assessment and finalizes their client recommendations and readout, the team holds a readout rehearsal with ATG leadership and relevant SMEs to practice and validate the project's story and final recommendations.

Project Closure activities may occur at different times depending on the exit scenario or next phase work, but the same set of activities must be completed to fully close out the project internally and with the client. These include final knowledge transfer, final deliverables handoff, go live notification, admin closure activities, project retrospective, case study creation, and finally, celebration!

labels.shortDescription: Gate 5: Project Closure & Next Phase Assessment
labels.value: Project Closure activities may occur at different times depending upon the plans for the next phase of work, but the same set of activities must be completed to fully close out the project internally and with the client. These include final knowledge transfer, final deliverables handoff, admin closure activities, case study creation, and finally, celebration!

Scope, Timeline & Budget Management activities occur throughout the entire lifecycle of the project. The Project Manager will perform weekly status reporting, governance log management, financial manager updates, delivery dashboard updates, and monthly invoicing and timesheet reconciliation in ESA. All team members are responsible for identifying any potential risks or issues to scope, timeline, and budget, and communicating them to the Project Manager. If necessary, the Project Manager will ultimately own client communication and/or Change Order creation.

Data Migration and Integrations workstreams run alongside the implementation project. Their development is highly dependent on the implementation, but the development and testing cadence will differ from the implementation sprints. Both workstreams will include multiple iterations of (1) discovery and planning, (2) design and data mapping, (3) development, and (4) execution and testing that must take place before migrating data or deploying integrations into a production system.

During Stage 0, the Sales Executive sources leads either directly, from a partner, or from Cognizant. They then work to understand the client's needs and evaluate whether ATG is a good fit to help them meet those needs.

During Stage 1, the Solution Engineer conducts scoping sessions, develops and delivers a proposal, completes an SOW, and staffs and engages the project team. Once engaged, the Project Manager begins setting up the project.

Throughout Stage 2, the delivery team conducts initial meetings internally and with the client. They prepare for and conduct workshop sessions, and use the information gathered to baseline key project and design deliverables. They should also begin evaluating requirement LOEs and assessing client readiness in preparation for the Project Success Confirmation.

Throughout Stage 2.5, the delivery team conducts initial meetings internally with the Project Team to review the estimation for the in-scope activities using the CoE estimation templates. With this, the delivery team can determine the deviation in effort (if any) as planned during the Sales Stage. Based on the outcome of this exercise Project Team will either decide to go ahead with baselining the effort and requirements or go for a SoW rewrite as necessary.

During Stage 2, the assessment team conducts both informal and formal kickoff sessions with the client to align on engagement success criteria, desired business outcomes, and the project plan, as well as to develop a meeting cadence with the client. Additionally, the team begins to identify and track client stakeholders.

During Stage 3, the delivery team works in iterative sprints which are typically two weeks long. Each sprint starts with sprint planning, and then the team splits into two workstreams. The Implementation Consultant and Quality Assurance Analyst work on building, testing, and demoing the requirements for that sprint. The Solution Architect and Business Analyst work to clarify requirements and design for the upcoming sprint. Each sprint closes with deliverable updates and client reviews, client knowledge transfers, and optionally retrospectives. Throughout this stage, planning conversations for UAT, SIT, Deployment, Data Migration and Integration should also occur.

During Stage 3, the assessment team reviews client artifacts and holds discovery sessions and stakeholder interviews. The team collects key observations and builds the client's current state EMF and architecture diagram based on discovery. The vision workshop is hosted with key client stakeholders to align on the project's vision and mission and the analysis of stakeholders level of understanding, commitment, and influence is completed. The team also begins developing initial themes based on discovery findings and forming the framework of their readout.

Stage 4 begins with ATG deploying configuration into a UAT environment. Depending on the project, a mock data migration and/or SIT testing may occur. Typically the client manages the UAT process, gathering, triaging, and prioritizing feedback and then passing defects to ATG to iteratively resolve. Responsibilities may depend based on the project.

During Stage 4, the assessment team finalizes key themes, maps observations to support those themes, and identifies gaps and opportunities based on current state. The team drafts, validates, and finalizes the client's future state EMF and architecture diagram and aligns with the client on business impacts and project KPIs. The team develops the vision statement, personas, a sponsor strategy and charter, and completes the change capability assessment. Findings and recommendations are drafted, along with continued development of the readout.

During Stage 5, the Deployment team or the delivery team deploys all configuration into the Production environment and performs a smoke test of the functionality. Depending on the project, a Data Migration into Production and deployment of Integrations may occur. Concurrently, the client works on user provisioning and change management activities. Once the system is live, a subset of the delivery team remains engaged to provide Hypercare Support to ensure the system is stable.

During Stage 6, the Application Support Specialist fields support tickets and assists in a variety of capacities to ensure that the client is successful in using and maintaining their solution. A SME remains available to assist the Application Support Specialist when needed.

During Stage 6, the assessment team onboards any new team members joining the next phase of work with the client, ensuring a smooth transition both internally and for the client. The assessment team also holds a final project retrospective.
Once validated with ATG leadership, the assessment team polishes their recommendations and hosts the client readout to share findings, recommendations, and a roadmap.
